examples.ko: 바람이 제 머리카락을 다 흩뜨려 놓았어요.
examples.en: The wind messed up all my hair.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 방 안에 다 흩뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The child scattered all the toys around the room.

examples.ko: 종이를 흩뜨리지 말고 한곳에 모아 두세요.
examples.en: Don't scatter the papers; keep them together in one place.

examples.ko: 옆 사람의 휴대폰 소리가 집중을 흩뜨려요.
examples.en: The sound of the person next to me's phone breaks my concentration.
What am I supposed to do if you mess up the tidy desk again?

examples.ko: 카드를 실수로 흩뜨리는 바람에 처음부터 다시 세었어요.
examples.en: I accidentally scattered the cards, so I had to count them again from the start.

explain: '흩트리다'로도 쓰고, 모여 있거나 정돈된 것을 어지럽게 만든다는 느낌이 강해요. 저절로 흩어지는 건 '흩어지다', 반대로 한곳에 두는 건 '모으다'예요. 머리카락이나 물건뿐 아니라 '집중, 분위기' 같은 추상적인 것에도 써요.
explain_en: It can also be written '흩트리다' and carries the feel of messing up something that was gathered or neat. Things that scatter by themselves use '흩어지다', and the opposite is '모으다' (to gather). It is used for hair and objects, and also for abstract things like concentration or atmosphere.

examples.en: The farmer scatters seeds over the field.
Rain sprinkled lightly from the morning and stopped soon after.
The children scattered flower petals on the road.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 가루 설탕을 살짝 흩뿌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please sprinkle a little powdered sugar on the cake.
I made a painting by flinging paint across the canvas.

examples.ko: 봄바람이 꽃가루를 흩뿌리는 바람에 재채기가 계속 나요.
examples.en: The spring wind is spreading pollen around, so I keep sneezing.

explain: 씨앗, 꽃잎, 가루, 물방울처럼 작은 것을 여기저기 넓게 뿌린다는 느낌이에요. 비나 눈이 가볍게 날릴 때 '비가 흩뿌리다'처럼 목적어 없이도 써요. 그냥 '뿌리다'보다 흩어지는 모습이 더 잘 그려져요.
explain_en: It gives the image of small things such as seeds, petals, powder or drops being spread widely here and there. It can also be used without an object, as in '비가 흩뿌리다' (rain drizzles in light sprays). Compared with plain '뿌리다', the scattering picture is clearer.

examples.en: I saw a faint whitish light in the fog.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 희끄무레해서 어디 아픈 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Your face looked pale, so I thought you were sick.
It's dawn, so the sky is still a dim whitish color.
A faint whitish stain was left on the wall.
What looks faintly white in the distance is a mountain.

examples.ko: 희끄무레한 옷을 입은 사람이 골목으로 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A person in pale clothes passed through the alley.

explain: '하얗다'처럼 또렷하게 흰 게 아니라 흐릿하고 칙칙하게 희다는 느낌이에요. 불빛, 하늘, 얼굴빛처럼 멀거나 어슴푸레한 것에 자주 어울려요. 비슷한 말로 '희뿌옇다', '희멀겋다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is not a crisp white like '하얗다' but a dull, faint whiteness. It fits lights, skies and complexions that are distant or dim. Similar words are '희뿌옇다' and '희멀겋다'.

examples.en: My hair has started to turn gray in patches.
Patches of snow are still left on the mountaintop.
Something white flashed by in the dark.
A person's shadow flickered past the window.
Frost has settled in white patches over the field.

examples.ko: 저고리는 희끗희끗 잔설이 녹는 마당 한가운데 떨어져 있었어요.
examples.en: The jacket lay in the middle of the yard where patches of old snow were melting.

explain: '희끗'은 한순간 희게 보이는 모양이고, '희끗희끗'은 군데군데 희게 섞여 있는 모양이에요. 흰머리나 남은 눈을 말할 때는 보통 '희끗희끗'을 써요. 형용사 '희끗희끗하다'로 '머리가 희끗희끗하다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: '희끗' shows something flashing white for a moment, while '희끗희끗' shows white mixed in here and there. For gray hair or leftover snow, people usually say '희끗희끗'. It also works as the adjective '희끗희끗하다', as in '머리가 희끗희끗하다'.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 희멀건 아이가 환하게 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: A pale-faced child is smiling brightly.
The broth is watery and pale like water.
After staying home for so long, my skin has turned pale and washed out.

examples.ko: 희멀건 죽만 먹었더니 힘이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: I only ate thin, pale porridge, so I have no energy at all.
Under the fluorescent light, your face looks pale and washed out.
A daytime moon hung in the dull, pale sky.

explain: 윤기 없이 멀겋고 하얀 느낌이라서 '예쁘게 하얗다'는 칭찬으로는 잘 안 써요. 피부, 국물, 죽, 하늘처럼 싱겁거나 맥없어 보이는 것에 어울려요. 활용은 '희멀건, 희멀게요, 희멀게졌어요'처럼 'ㅎ'이 빠져요.
explain_en: It suggests a lifeless, washed-out white, so it is rarely used as a compliment for pretty fairness. It fits skin, broth, porridge or sky that looks thin or listless. The 'ㅎ' drops in conjugation: 희멀건, 희멀게요, 희멀게졌어요.

examples.ko: 화난 사람이 눈을 희번덕거리며 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The angry man glared at me, rolling his eyes wildly.
The cat's eyes keep flashing in the dark.
Please don't roll your eyes like that. It's scary.

examples.ko: 그는 눈알을 희번덕거리면서 큰 소리로 말했어요.
examples.en: He spoke loudly, his eyeballs rolling about.
My younger brother rolled his eyes around as a joke.

examples.ko: 영화 속 악당이 눈을 희번덕거려서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The villain in the movie rolled his eyes wildly, and it was scary.

explain: 눈을 크게 뜨고 번득이며 굴리는 모습이라 놀람, 분노, 이상한 흥분 같은 센 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '눈을 희번덕거리다'로 쓰고, '희번덕대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '눈을 부라리다'나 '눈을 굴리다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes widely opened eyes flashing and rolling, so it has a strong feel of shock, anger or odd excitement. It is mostly used as '눈을 희번덕거리다', and '희번덕대다' means the same. In daily speech, '눈을 부라리다' or '눈을 굴리다' is more common.

examples.en: It's foggy, so everything ahead is hazy.
The night sky turned hazy, as if it were about to snow.
The room is full of hazy white smoke.

examples.ko: 미세먼지 때문에 창밖이 온통 희뿌예서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of fine dust, everything outside is hazy and I can't see anything.
My glasses fogged up when I came out of the bathroom.
The dawn sky was hazy at first and gradually grew brighter.

explain: 안개, 연기, 먼지 때문에 앞이 뿌옇고 허옇게 보일 때 써요. 그냥 '뿌옇다'보다 흰빛이 도는 느낌이 더 있어요. 활용은 '희뿌예요, 희뿌연, 희뿌옇게'로 'ㅎ'이 빠져요.
explain_en: Use it when fog, smoke or dust makes things look blurry with a whitish tint. Compared with plain '뿌옇다', it has more of a white cast. The 'ㅎ' drops in conjugation: 희뿌예요, 희뿌연, 희뿌옇게.

examples.ko: 합격 소식을 들은 어머니 얼굴이 희색으로 가득했어요.
examples.en: My mother's face was full of joy when she heard I had passed.

examples.ko: 아이가 선물을 받고 얼굴에 희색을 띠었어요.
examples.en: The child's face lit up after receiving the present.
The beaming groom greeted the guests.

examples.ko: 결과를 듣고도 선생님 얼굴에 희색은 보이지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after hearing the results, there was no look of joy on the teacher's face.

examples.ko: 희색이 도는 얼굴을 보니 좋은 소식인 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Seeing your delighted face, I figured it was good news.

examples.ko: 아버지는 희색 가득한 얼굴로 집에 돌아오셨어요.
examples.en: My father came home with a face full of happiness.

explain: 기쁜 마음이 얼굴빛에 드러난 것을 말해서, 보통 '희색이 돌다, 희색을 띠다, 희색이 가득하다'처럼 얼굴과 함께 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 대화에서는 '표정이 밝다', '얼굴이 환해지다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to joy showing in someone's complexion and expression, so it typically goes with the face: '희색이 돌다', '희색을 띠다', '희색이 가득하다'. It appears more in writing and news than in everyday talk. In conversation people more often say '표정이 밝다' or '얼굴이 환해지다'.

examples.en: That village became a victim of the war.

examples.ko: 어른들 싸움에 아이들을 희생물로 삼으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't make children the victims of adults' fights.
He was a victim of a false rumor.

examples.ko: 유행의 희생물이 되지 않으려면 스스로 판단해야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid becoming a victim of trends, you have to judge for yourself.
When the company ran into trouble, he was pushed out like a scapegoat.

examples.ko: 개발의 희생물인 오래된 골목을 지키자는 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: People started talking about protecting the old alley that fell victim to development.

explain: '~의 희생물이 되다'처럼 어떤 힘이나 상황 때문에 피해를 보는 사람이나 것에 써요. 비슷한 '희생양'은 남의 잘못을 대신 떠안는 느낌이 더 강해요. '희생자'는 사람에게만 쓰는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used in '~의 희생물이 되다' for a person or thing that suffers because of some force or situation. The similar '희생양' stresses taking the blame for others more strongly. '희생자', by contrast, refers only to people.

examples.ko: 이 우표는 희소성 때문에 값이 아주 비싸요.
examples.en: This stamp is very expensive because of its rarity.
The higher an item's scarcity, the higher its price.
We learned the concept of scarcity in economics class.

examples.ko: 희소성도 물건의 가치를 만드는 한 가지 이유예요.
examples.en: Rarity is also one reason that gives an item its value.

examples.ko: 자원의 희소성에 비해 사람들의 욕구는 끝이 없어요.
examples.en: Compared with the scarcity of resources, people's wants are endless.

examples.ko: 희소성만으로 물건의 가치를 정할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't decide an item's value by rarity alone.

explain: '희소성이 높다/있다/크다'처럼 쓰고, 가지고 싶은 것에 비해 수가 적다는 점을 말해요. 경제 수업의 '희소성'과 일상의 '귀하다'가 이어지지만, 일상에서는 '귀하다', '구하기 어렵다'를 더 많이 말해요. 한정판이나 수집품 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used as '희소성이 높다/있다/크다' and points to there being few of something compared with how much people want it. The economics term connects to everyday '귀하다', but in daily talk people say '귀하다' or '구하기 어렵다' more. It often comes up with limited editions and collectibles.

examples.en: I went out to have fun with my friends, laughing and cheerful.
The children are happily playing around in the snow.
Don't be too jubilant just because the exam is over.

examples.ko: 복권에 당첨된 줄 알고 한참 희희낙락했어요.
examples.en: I thought I had won the lottery and was giddy with joy for a while.

examples.ko: 일은 안 하고 계속 희희낙락하면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are we supposed to do if you keep giggling and don't work?
My older brother is wandering around all cheerful, even though he doesn't know the result.

explain: '즐겁다, 신나다'보다 들뜬 모습으로 웃고 떠드는 느낌이 강해요. 때로는 상황을 모르고 철없이 좋아하는 사람을 못마땅하게 볼 때도 써요. '희희낙락거리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It carries a stronger feel of laughing and chatting in high spirits than '즐겁다' or '신나다'. It is sometimes used with mild disapproval for someone who is carelessly happy without understanding the situation. It can also be said as '희희낙락거리다'.

en: bluffing; bragging; big talk; hot air

examples.en: My uncle spouts big talk whenever we meet.
Stop talking big and get to work.
Everything he said was just hot air.
Don't brag; show me yourself.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 흰소리만 치고 약속은 안 지켜요.
examples.en: That friend only talks big and doesn't keep promises.

examples.ko: 흰소리로 들리겠지만 저는 정말 일등 할 거예요.
examples.en: It may sound like bragging, but I really am going to take first place.

explain: 실제로는 못 할 일을 크게 떠벌릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. '흰소리를 치다, 흰소리를 늘어놓다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '허풍', '큰소리'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes loudly boasting about things one can't really do. People say '흰소리를 치다' or '흰소리를 늘어놓다'. In daily speech, '허풍' and '큰소리' are more common.

examples.ko: 동생이 시험 때문에 요즘 히스테리를 부려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been throwing fits lately because of exams.
I got so stressed that my fits of temper got worse.

examples.ko: 별일 아닌데 히스테리까지 부릴 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: It's no big deal, so there's no need to throw a fit.

examples.ko: 그 상사의 히스테리 때문에 직원들이 힘들어해요.
examples.en: The staff are struggling because of that boss's tantrums.

examples.ko: 갑자기 소리를 지르는 게 꼭 히스테리처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: Suddenly screaming looked just like a hysterical outburst.

examples.ko: 그건 화가 난 게 아니라 일종의 히스테리예요.
examples.en: That isn't anger; it's a kind of hysterical outburst.

explain: 일상에서는 '히스테리를 부리다'처럼 감정이 격해져 갑자기 짜증 내거나 소리 지르는 모습에 써요. 병명으로 쓰는 말과 느낌이 달라서, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '신경질'이 있어요.
explain_en: In daily life it is used in '히스테리를 부리다' for suddenly snapping or screaming when emotions run high. It feels different from the medical term, and saying it directly to someone can sound rude. A similar word is '신경질'.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 얼굴을 보더니 히죽 웃었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling looked at my face and grinned.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 히죽 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just grinned without saying a word.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 들은 아이가 히죽 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child who was praised let out a grin.

examples.ko: 혼자 히죽 웃는 걸 보니 좋은 일이 있나 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you grinning to yourself, something good must have happened.

examples.ko: 친구가 히죽이 웃는 얼굴로 한마디 했어요.
examples.en: My friend said a word with a grin on his face.

examples.ko: 히죽 웃고 있는 친구에게 무슨 일이냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: I asked my grinning friend what was going on.

explain: 입을 한쪽으로 살짝 벌리고 흐뭇하거나 능글맞게 웃는 모습이에요. '빙긋'보다 속없어 보이거나 장난스러운 느낌이 있어요. 센 느낌의 '히쭉'도 있고, 계속 웃을 때는 '히죽히죽'을 써요.
explain_en: It shows a smile with the mouth opening slightly, either contentedly or slyly. Compared with '빙긋', it can seem a bit goofy or mischievous. There is also the stronger '히쭉', and '히죽히죽' is used when someone keeps grinning.

en: grin; give one contented smile after another

examples.en: Why have you been grinning to yourself over and over since earlier?

examples.ko: 친구가 휴대폰을 보며 계속 히죽거리고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend keeps grinning while looking at the phone.
Stop smirking and tell me the reason.
My younger brother grinned when he saw his test score.
Even when he was teased, he just grinned and let it pass.
The way he was smirking was a bit annoying.

explain: 혼자 흐뭇해서, 또는 능글맞게 자꾸 웃는 모습이에요. 기분 좋은 일이 있을 때도 쓰지만 상대에게 쓰면 '실실 웃는다'는 비꼬는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. '히죽대다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes smiling repeatedly, either from private satisfaction or in a sly way. It can be used for happy moments, but said about someone else it can sound like a mocking 'smirking around'. It can also be said as '히죽대다'.
